==English==
{{wp|+ (business)}}
{{wp|+ (computing)}}
{{wp|+ state}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ḱlew-|*ḱley-|id2=incline}}
From {{inh|en|enm|client}}, from {{der|en|xno|clyent}}, {{der|en|fro|client}}, from {{der|en|la|cliēns}}, akin to {{m|la|clinare|t=to lean}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈklaɪ.ənt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-client.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyphenation|en|cli|ent}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪənt|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[customer]], a buyer or receiver of [[goods]] or [[service]]s.
#: {{syn|en|buyer|customer|patron|purchaser}}
# {{lb|en|computing}} The role of a [[computer]] [[application]] or [[system]] that requests and/or consumes the services provided by another having the role of [[server]].
#: {{ant|en|server}}
# A person who receives help or services from a [[professional]] such as a [[lawyer]] or [[accountant]].
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=I corralled the judge, and we started off across the fields{{...}}. And thus we came by a circuitous route to Mohair,{{...}}. My '''client''' welcomed the judge […] and they disappeared together into the Ethiopian card-room, which was filled with the assegais and exclamation point shields Mr. Cooke had had made at the sawmill at Beaverton.}}
# {{lb|en|legal}} A person who employs or retains an attorney to represent him or her in any legal matter, or one who merely divulges confidential matters to an attorney while pursuing professional assistance without subsequently retaining the attorney.
# {{lb|en|historical}} In ancient Rome, [[retainer]]s and [[follower]]s associated with a [[gens]].
#* {{RQ:Withycombe Christian Names|edition=1st|chapter=Introduction|page=xv|passage=The nomen belonged to all members of a ''gens'' and to all those attached to it (women, '''clients''', and freedmen included).}}
# {{lb|en|international relations}} {{ellipsis of|en|client state}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1989|author=Edward A. Kolodziej; Roger E. Kanet|title=Limits of Soviet Power|page=95
|passage=A third preliminary comment deals explicitly with the relations between '''clients''' and superpowers.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Simon Tisdall|title=Russia is losing the war in Ukraine, and Putin is desperate. But that’s when he’s at his most dangerous|date=2026-06-14|url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/jun/14/vladimir-putin-ukraine-war-borders-russian-president|passage=Russia’s leader is a conservative, old-school thug. He thinks Russia is still a superpower, not what he’s made it: a despised rogue state and Chinese '''client'''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261024014106/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/jun/14/vladimir-putin-ukraine-war-borders-russian-president|archivedate=24 October 2026}}
